Nov 7 : Elena Rybakina's withdrawal from the WTA Finals on the eve of the season-ending championships is disappointing, but the world number one needs time to recover from the physical toll of a demanding year, tournament director Garbine Muguruza said. Defending champion Rybakina pulled out of the tournament on Saturday, saying she was not physically ready to compete, leaving Ukraine's Marta Kostyuk to take her place in the eight-player field at Indian Wells. Muguruza, the former world number one and two-time Grand Slam champion, said she had spoken with Rybakina and that the Kazakh had been unable to recover in time after struggling with physical problems late in the season. "We love Elena and we know that she was feeling so-so in Tokyo as well," Muguruza told Reuters. "I spoke to her today and she really couldn't recover on time.

"What we want is for her to feel good, to go rest, to recover. We don't want her to feel like she has to play — only if she's ready to." Rybakina, who won two Grand Slam titles this year, also withdrew from the Tokyo quarter-finals last month because of a neck injury. 'AMAZING FIELD' Rybakina's absence deprives the event of some star power, but Muguruza said the round-robin format and depth of the field would ensure a high-quality tournament. "We have the best players," said Muguruza, who triumphed at the WTA Finals in Guadalajara in 2021.  "I know our world number one is not going to be able to play, but we have an amazing field, the very best. "Every match could be a Grand Slam final. You really need to be ready. You cannot give one inch." Kostyuk, who is making her WTA Finals debut after a breakthrough season that included the Madrid title and a rise into the top 10, was already in Indian Wells as an alternate and practicing when Rybakina withdrew. Muguruza said the Ukrainian, known for her signature post-match backflip celebrations, had earned her opportunity. "Marta is great. She's had a breakthrough year," Muguruza said. "With this year, we have many first-time players in the Finals, and that's very exciting. It's very hard to qualify." Kostyuk has been outspoken about Russia's invasion of Ukraine and does not shake hands with Russian or Belarusian opponents. Muguruza said the tournament would support players in making their own decisions. "They're free to do whatever they feel," she said. "We are open and supporting them." OPPORTUNITY FOR SABALENKA  Rybakina's withdrawal could create an opening for world number two Aryna Sabalenka to make inroads in the rankings.  Sabalenka, who won the Indian Wells title earlier this year, has the chance to reduce the gap with Rybakina at the top of the rankings, Muguruza said, while also highlighting Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva as a player comfortable in the California desert. "Of course, Aryna might be thinking that this can be a good opportunity," Muguruza said. The WTA moved the Finals to Indian Wells from Riyadh, with Muguruza saying player safety had been the decisive consideration amid conflict in the region. "It clearly felt no longer safe to be in a region where there is conflict," she said. "Taking care of the players and looking ahead to what could be safe, comfortable and secure, relocating felt the best decision." Muguruza said players had responded positively to the switch to Indian Wells, where she competed regularly during her career. "When we knew that Indian Wells could be the next venue, it was just a joy," she said, adding that ticket sales have been strong. "The whole thing is just perfect."

Source: Reuters

SAO PAULO, Nov 7 : Ferrari teammates Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc said they had put last weekend's Mexico City Grand Prix controversy behind them after holding talks aimed at easing tensions following their opening-lap clash. The pair met with team principal Frederic Vasseur this week after their battle derailed Ferrari's hopes of a one-two finish and prompted Hamilton to publicly criticise the way the race unfolded. Vasseur said on Friday that the discussions had been productive and that Ferrari had "turned the page", while Hamilton had insisted earlier in the week that he would not apologise for speaking openly about his frustrations. After qualifying for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix on Saturday, both drivers struck a conciliatory tone and said the matter was now closed.

"From my perspective, I was very straightforward, of course, and I think it was good to speak," Leclerc told reporters at Interlagos about the incident which he felt had been blown out of proportion. The Monegasque, who became a father this week, said the timing of the discussions had been affected by personal commitments but that talking face-to-face had helped resolve the issue. "Now I consider that a closed chapter, and I think it will be important to look ahead," he said. Hamilton echoed that view, saying the conversation had allowed both drivers to air their perspectives before moving on. "We sat and spoke and we squashed it and we're moving on," the seven-times world champion said. "I think we still have a huge amount of respect for each other. I'm glad we had a chat and now we move on. We've been getting along just fine as normal." The Briton added that neither side had made demands during the talks and that the focus had been on working together more effectively. Leclerc was fourth fastest in qualifying but will drop 10 places on the grid for Sunday's race because of power unit changes, while Hamilton will start from the back after accumulating engine penalties totalling 65 places, prompting Ferrari to stop his participation after the first phase of qualifying.

Source: Reuters

SAO PAULO, Nov 7 : Brazilian drivers endured a torrid, rain-hit qualifying session for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix on Saturday as Gabriel Bortoleto finished last and F1 debutant Rafael Camara qualified 13th, dampening the excitement surrounding Brazil's first home driver pairing at Interlagos in a decade. Audi's Bortoleto slid into the barriers in Q1, reviving memories of last year's nightmare when he retired on the opening lap of his first home Grand Prix after an earlier sprint crash. "Right now, (it feels like) shit. I mean,. what can I say? Last year, I had a crash. This year, I couldn't do qualifying properly because I messed up. "So yeah, it looks like home race for me hasn't been good yet," Bortoleto told reporters, adding he would clear his head and try to put together a strong performance on Sunday.

Camara, making his Formula One debut for Haas after replacing Frenchman Esteban Ocon, spun in Q1 and recovered, only to lose control later in the session and hit the wall. Camara described it as a chaotic qualifying session but played down the incident, saying the support from the home crowd helped him keep a positive mindset despite the setback. "I think it’s another learning experience for tomorrow. Of course, it’s not ideal, but you end up understanding more and preparing yourself much better." Both Brazilians gained places on the grid after qualifying, as penalties reshuffled the starting order. Max Verstappen, Sergio Perez and Lewis Hamilton were already set to start from the back after taking additional power unit components, promoting Bortoleto to 19th. Charles Leclerc, who qualified ahead of Camara, will also drop behind the Brazilian due to a penalty, leaving the Haas driver set to start 11th.

SAO PAULO, Nov 7 : George Russell raged over the radio after the Mercedes driver was thwarted in a bid for a morale-boosting fastest lap in Sao Paulo Grand Prix qualifying on Saturday. Russell carried a five-place grid penalty for an engine change but the Briton still wanted to finish the session on top. Instead, he was told to back off after coming up behind Williams' Alex Albon and the rain then denied him any further chance of beating the pole time set by McLaren's Lando Norris. "Mate, you told me to back off! What the hell?," Russell shouted over the radio after realising his day was done and he was only second fastest and would be seventh on the grid. "P2. I don't want to be P2. I want to be P1."

Team boss Toto Wolff said it was a 50-50 call and Russell, after so many ups and downs this season, had been in league of his own. "I don't think it would have been enough for pole, but he drove perfectly all session and merited to be on pole," said the Austrian of the aborted lap. "He deserved it but you can't make that call. It's 50 per cent right or wrong. Russell's teammate Kimi Antonelli clinched the title at the previous race in Mexico City and the Briton is now fourth in the battle for overall runner-up after starting the season as title favourite. "That was definitely the pole lap," the 28-year-old said later. "Misjudgement on our side. Need to understand what happened as obviously the rain was coming and we should have just finished the lap. "It depends on the weather," he said of his prospects on Sunday. "I mean, I felt good out there. It's the first time in a while I've felt confident in the car. I felt more confident in the wet than I do in the dry, I don't really understand why that was. "I felt more like myself... unfortunately when it mattered we didn't execute." Russell took the first win of his F1 career at Interlagos in 2022. McLaren team boss Andre Stella acknowledged that the Briton was "probably the fastest car" in the third phase of qualifying. "I saw that he was not impeded, but he just found Albon, and he couldn't close his second lap on inters, which I think up until that point was on par with pole position, if not faster," Stella told reporters.

(Writing by Alan Baldwin in London, editing by Pritha Sarkar)

Source: Reuters

ROME, Nov 7 : AS Roma moved to second in the Serie A standings with a 3-0 win over struggling Sassuolo at the Stadio Olimpico on Saturday, where the league's highest scoring side underlined their title credentials and had little trouble seeing off the club with the worst defensive record. Roma maintained their unbeaten start to the season and are on 27 points, one behind leaders Lazio - the only other Serie A side yet to lose - and two ahead of third-placed Inter Milan. Lazio are away to Napoli on Sunday and Inter host fourth-placed Como. Sassuolo held out until the 27th minute when Roma defender Mario Hermoso drove forward towards the area. His attempted pass to Donyell Malen was intercepted but he gathered the loose ball, took a touch to make space and fired into the roof of the net. Three minutes later, Malen's shot took a touch off a Sassuolo defender before Sebastian Walukiewicz turned the ball into his own net.

Sassuolo keeper Arijanet Muric kept his side in the game with saves from Leonardo Balerdi and Matias Soule before the break but Rodrigo Mora's 58th-minute goal put the game out of reach. GOALS GALORE FOR GASPERINI'S ROMA Roma have scored 31 goals in their 11 league games, while Sassuolo have conceded 29. The visitors came into Saturday’s meeting having shipped 10 goals in their previous two matches and were one place and one point above the relegation zone. Malen may not have added to his goal tally, but is proving invaluable to Gian Piero Gasperini's side. The Dutch striker has eight league goals this campaign, along with four in the Champions League as he continues where he left off last season. He joined Roma on loan from Aston Villa in January, and after netting 14 goals in 18 league games, the Italian club made his move permanent in May. The last time Roma won the title was in 2001, while Lazio's most recent success came the season before that, and the Scudetto could well make its long-awaited return to the capital as the rivals continue to prove unstoppable this season. Elsewhere, Bologna moved to eighth in the standings on 17 points with a 2-1 win away to 10-man Parma, one point ahead of Cagliari who earned a 1-0 victory over Frosinone. Torino were held to a 1-1 draw at home by Lecce, with both sides scoring via an own goal.

PARIS, Nov 7 : The French capital has rarely enjoyed such soccer hegemony but two Parisian clubs sit on top of the Ligue 1 standings after victories on Saturday. That European champions Paris St Germain head the standings is no surprise as their 1-0 home win over Troyes at the Parc de Princes extended their winning streak to 11 games across all competitions. But neighbours Paris FC sitting three points behind them was not expected as they are only in their second season in the top flight. Paris FC won 1-0 at Auxerre in Saturday’s earlier game to move into second spot with 20 points from 10 games, striker Lassine Sinayoko netting his ninth league goal of the season.

Sinayoko was facing his former club and there was a touch of fortune about his winner as he stretched out a leg to get a touch on a mis-hit shot from Pablo Pagis in the 63rd minute. PSG have 23 points as they continued to shrug off their early season lethargy with Ukraine defender Ilya Zabarnyi heading home the winner against Troyes six minutes before halftime. KONATE KEEPS PSG AT BAY There were opportunities for a more convincing scoreline but visiting goalkeeper Hillel Konate kept at bay the PSG attack, which plundered six goals at Villarreal in the Champions League on Tuesday. Paris FC’s promotion last season meant there were two clubs from the capital in the top division for the first time in 35 years. To spice up the rivalry they moved their home from the south edge of the city at Charlety to Stade Jean-Bouin, a 19,600-capacity rugby ground across the street from the Parc de Princes. They finished 11th last season, ending their fixtures with a 2-1 home victory over PSG having also knocked them out of the French Cup. Paris FC's fortunes have been boosted this season with the arrival both of coach Liam Rosenior, manager of Chelsea last season, and Mali international Sinayoko. "Lassine has been exceptional since the start of the season," Rosenior said last week after they beat Monaco 3-1. "People remember his goals, but we have also worked a lot on his positioning. He has understood what we wanted from him, and he deserves the credit."

(Writing by Mark Gleeson in Cape Town; Editing by Ed Osmond)

Nov 7 : Real Madrid cruised to a 3-0 win at struggling Valencia in LaLiga on Saturday as Federico Valverde, Arda Guler and Kylian Mbappe scored to move the visitors level with leaders Barcelona. Real have 30 points alongside Barca, who lead on goal difference and have a game in hand. Barcelona visit third-placed Atletico Madrid on Sunday, with the hosts two points behind and able to leapfrog both rivals with victory. It was Real's eighth consecutive win, another confident, efficient display building on their El Clasico victory at the Camp Nou two weeks ago. With Vinicius Jr serving the final match of a four-game ban for pulling an opponent's hair and protesting to the referee, manager Jose Mourinho again deployed Yan Diomande on the left wing alongside Mbappe in attack.

Guler, Jude Bellingham, Bernardo Silva and Aurelien Tchouameni formed the midfield, while captain Valverde, a midfielder by trade, continued at right back. Real's opening goals underlined their threat from different areas, with the Uruguayan striking from distance and Guler finding space inside the box. Valverde broke the deadlock in the 28th minute with a fierce half-volley after Mbappe's shot rebounded off a defender, his low drive flying just inside the left post. Real doubled their advantage eight minutes later when Bellingham's deflected cross found Guler unmarked, the Turkey international finishing first time from close range. Valencia repeatedly resorted to heavy challenges to halt the visitors, but Real added a third in the 75th minute. Guler turned provider, slipping the ball to Mbappe inside the box, where the French striker rounded the advancing goalkeeper and tapped into the empty net. Valencia captain Jose Gaya was sent off five minutes later for a fierce tackle on Mbappe, completing a miserable evening for the hosts. Javier Aguirre's Valencia are second-bottom on nine points, with only two wins in 12 league matches and none at home this season.

LYON, France Nov 7 : Injury-hit France crushed Fiji 54-17 in Lyon on Saturday to return to the top of the Northern Hemisphere section of the Nations Championship before facing South Africa. The French side scored eight tries through Jean-Baptiste Gros, Sipili Falatea, Aaron Grandidier Nkanang, Kalvin Gourgues, Theo Attissogbe, Charles Ollivon, Antoine Dupont and a penalty try. Gourgues and Maxime Lucu added 12 points with the boot. Vinaya Habosi and Selestino Ravutaumada scored Fiji’s two tries, both converted by Ben Volavola. France are on 17 points, two clear of Ireland, but lost flyhalf Romain Ntamack to injury during the first half.

Fiji are bottom of the Southern Hemisphere section without a point before heading to Ireland next week. Despite missing a string of players, including flyhalf Matthieu Jalibert and fullback Thomas Ramos, France managed to secure a third win in four matches in the new competition. "We are very happy with the result," Attissogbe told TF1. "We knew it was important to take the win, given the results of the other nations. We are carrying on with our momentum." EARLY ERRORS The match started shakily for France with a series of early errors, but Gros settled their nerves by powering over in the 15th minute. The forwards dominated the first half, with a penalty try awarded after a driving maul led to Isoa Nasilasila's yellow card. Eleven minutes later, tighthead prop Falatea ended a long attacking move, seconds after Ntamack injured his shoulder.  Winger Grandidier Nkanang claimed the bonus point just before halftime, capitalising on an interception mistake by Vilimoni Botitu to send France into the break with a commanding 26-3 lead. Fiji's only first-half points came from a Simione Kuruvoli penalty. The second half continued in the same vein, though France endured a scrappy 20-minute spell before Gourgues and Attissogbe, finishing off a slick counter-attack started by Antoine Dupont and continued by Louis Bielle-Biarrey, added tries in quick succession. Attack dominated the last quarter, with two tries for each side. Fiji responded with a solo effort from Habosi, who beat four defenders to cross the line and Ravutaumada finished under the posts. Charles Ollivon powered over and Dupont crossed for France’s seventh and eighth tries. French celebrations were dampened by Ntamack’s injury ahead of their next game against world champions South Africa. "Romain (Ntamack) came off after that injury and we won’t have him for the rest of the competition," France coach Fabien Galthie told TF1. "An examination revealed a fairly serious shoulder injury."

Source: Reuters
